news.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
news.summary_raw: Discover how Sophos uses OpenAI’s Daybreak to cut cyber-threat investigation time by 96% and automate 52% of MDR cases while preserving human oversight.
news.summary: Sophos has integrated OpenAI’s Daybreak model into its MDR platform, slashing threat investigation time by 96% and automating 52% of cases while retaining human oversight.
news.enterprise_use: Go to the Sophos MDR console this week and enable the Daybreak integration under the Investigation Automation settings. Failure to adopt could leave your team spending hours on manual triage and missing emerging threats faster than competitors. This directly impacts your endpoint security stack, especially where CrowdStrike or other MDR solutions are evaluated for future upgrades.

news.title: Rehearsal Intelligence: Using Digital Twins for Crisis Readiness
news.summary_raw: Carolyn Geason-Beissel/MIT SMR | Getty Images In July 2024, the cybersecurity software company CrowdStrike pushed a routine but buggy software update to its platform. In the ensuing 78 minutes, before a patch was deployed, IT systems worldwide crashed. Microsoft estimated that 8.5 million Windows devices were affected. As blue screens of death cascaded across the […]
news.summary: CrowdStrike released a buggy software update that caused widespread system crashes affecting millions of Windows devices. The incident exposed a critical vulnerability in CrowdStrike’s endpoint protection platform.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Immediately review CrowdStrike policies and update the endpoint protection agents to the latest patch. S2: Failure to act risks continued downtime and potential data exfiltration on all managed devices. S3: The CrowdStrike platform is a core component of your endpoint security stack, so prioritizing this update is essential.

The release indicates a shift toward more advanced AI capabilities that could soon be integrated into Google’s suite of productivity tools.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Review the new Gemini 4 API documentation this week and assess whether the model can be leveraged to automate routine support tickets in Freshservice or enhance policy recommendations in JumpCloud. S2: Not integrating early could leave your organization behind competitors who start using Gemini‑powered analytics for user behavior insights, potentially exposing your SSO and MDM layers to newer attack vectors. S3: The most immediate impact will be on your Google Workspace and JumpCloud environments, where AI‑driven automation can streamline access management and incident response.

news.title: When Compliance Workarounds Backfire
news.summary_raw: John Holcroft/Ikon Images In 2021, Barcelona-based delivery platform Glovo was faced with a law that threatened its business model. Spain had passed the Rider Law, which introduced a presumption of employment when a digital platform organizes, directs, or controls couriers’ work, including through algorithmic management. Glovo came up with what seemed like a clever fix […]
news.summary: Spain’s new Rider Law imposes employment status on gig couriers when platforms use algorithmic management, forcing companies like Glovo to alter their business models. The regulation challenges the use of AI-driven scheduling and control systems that are common in modern workforce management.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Monitor your internal workforce scheduling and monitoring tools for AI-driven decision logic that might now be viewed as employment control. S2: Failure to adjust could expose your organization to legal risk, potential fines, and loss of operational flexibility.

news.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
news.summary_raw:
Training AI agents with reinforcement learning can be challenging because their tools, context, and decision-making are managed by complex frameworks. Agent Lightning connects existing agents to RL training, making it easier to improve them without rebuilding them.
The post Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released Agent Lightning v1.0, a lightweight 3,500‑line framework that connects existing AI agents to reinforcement learning pipelines, enabling easier training without extensive rewrites. The tool focuses on simplifying the integration of agents with real‑world environments and harnesses.
news.enterprise_use: Check your Microsoft Azure ML or other AI development environments for compatibility with Agent Lightning if you plan to experiment with RL training. Inaction means missing an opportunity to accelerate agent training with a streamlined, open‑source framework.

news.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
news.summary_raw:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.
The post Forecasting space weather risks on power grids appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has unveiled a machine learning system that can predict space‑weather events affecting power grids 30‑60 minutes in advance. The technology could improve resilience for critical infrastructure relying on GPS and satellite communications.
news.enterprise_use: Keep an eye on this development for the next 30 days to assess whether your organization’s power‑grid dependencies (e.g., data centers, satellite‑based backups) might benefit from early warning signals. Consider evaluating the tool’s integration potential with your existing monitoring dashboards to enhance predictive maintenance.

news.title: The Real Reasons Why Digital Projects Fail
news.summary_raw: Danae Diaz/Ikon Images It’s a familiar scenario: An organization implements digital tools intended to improve a particular process but fails to obtain the desired result. Employees who are meant to use them complain that the tools don’t solve the problem or that they add inefficiencies. Managers who investigate problems with the tools chalk the failure […]
news.summary: A recent MIT Sloan article discusses why digital projects often fail, highlighting user adoption issues, unclear goals, and misaligned technology choices. It emphasizes the importance of aligning tools with business needs and engaging end users early to avoid wasted investments.
news.enterprise_use: Check that any new IT initiatives you plan—such as updates to Google Workspace or JumpCloud configurations—have clear user requirements documented and pilot-tested with a small group before full roll-out. Failing to do so risks wasting resources and causing user frustration.

news.title: What AI gets wrong and what failure teaches us
news.summary_raw:
Jennifer Neville did not want to go into computer science—but that’s exactly where she landed. Neville discusses the starts and stops that led to her professional sweet spot and her work identifying “surprising failures” making it hard for AI to handle complexity. 
The post What AI gets wrong and what failure teaches us appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research released an analysis titled "What AI gets wrong and what failure teaches us," focusing on the unexpected failures that hinder AI from handling complex tasks. The study highlights the importance of understanding AI limitations rather than relying on model performance alone.
news.enterprise_use: Review the research to better anticipate AI-related risks in your environment; use its findings to refine monitoring and alerting for AI-enabled services such as Google Workspace or JumpCloud.
